And there are Dionysuses: the Theban; another, the son of Semele; the one among the Corybantes; the one torn apart by the Titans; and the one of the Curetes who initiates people into the distribution of flesh.

And Heracles, whom they call the averter of evil: I shall pass over in silence his many deeds, but out of them all I shall point out one which is perhaps praised among them. It was enough for him to undergo this labor so that salvation might come to the world! For if he had not deflowered fifty virgins in one night, how would the world have been saved? Rather, it would have perished!
In short, I confess to you, I am weary of writing out their wicked deeds in detail.

Moreover, kings and most savage tyrants who had certain favorites, after burying them in the [earth ?], having nothing more to bestow on them (being themselves as mortal as they were), out of affection for them handed down their tombs to their own subjects to be worshipped as those of gods, to the deception of mankind and on a wicked pretext. Such was Antinous, buried in Antinoë,

who, having lain in a pleasure barge, was thus enrolled [among the gods] by Hadrian. Timogenes is worshipped in Asia; Canopus, the helmsman of Menelaus, and his wife Eumenuthis, buried at Alexandria, are honored on the seashore, twelve milestones away; Marnas, a slave of Asterius the Cretan, is honored among the people of Gaza; and Basius the shipmaster among the people of Pelusium.

107. So when you teach all these things carefully in the midst of the church, you free those who have been led on in this way from the evil example of the road to death [?]. You bring others from adultery to chastity. You not only rid them of secret adultery, but also teach them, through continence, to disregard their own wives, since "the time has been shortened," as the holy apostle says. And you instruct fornicators, so that they may not be punished for having committed a deed unlawful before God and men.

And when you have toiled to hand on all these things by word and by deed, persuade them to accept everything from you. Do everything in practice first and shape it in yourselves, making your words believable through the actions by which you first taught yourselves, so that you may also make disciples of others.
For even when you are silent you shine forth like the sun, which teaches everyone everywhere even in silence. As soon as it rises, it silently teaches all people their crafts.

And when you hand on the benefit of all these things to your own children, or to your most faithful brothers, lead them on to walk upon the earth but to have their "citizenship in heaven," and stir up in most of them a zeal for the life of monks.

Through your steadfastness and unfeigned faith, you abhor the heretics, muzzle the Manichaeans, the Marcionites and others like them, and drive them out of God's church [?], undoing and silencing all their pretexts.

For how many things they boldly utter against God and against his holy prophets, frivolous as they are and empty of the Holy Spirit! They blaspheme the Creator of all things. All the good things that God graciously gave to all people through his holy prophets, by prophecy in the Spirit, these they hate. And the deepest things of the law and the prophets they do not understand, since they are earthly and carnal and judge in a merely natural way. But their blasphemy is in vain.
Do not hesitate to shake their error off your hearers at once, refuting them with true proofs. For by such words the empty-minded are swept away like brushwood in the current of a full river.

108. Suppose they say: "A fine God, the God of the law! He did not know where Adam was, and asked, 'Adam, where are you?' He says to Cain, 'Where is Abel your brother?' and to Abraham, 'Where is Sarah your wife?'" And they say many other such things.

But those who say such things believe in God the Savior with their mouths and not in truth. He is God and has foreknowledge, yet he asks questions just as in the Old Testament: "Where have you laid Lazarus?" and "Who touched me?" and "Do you have loaves with you?" and "Whom do you want?" or "Whom are you seeking?"

So the refutation of these people is easy and simple. Just as the Son asks questions although he has foreknowledge, so too the Father himself asks questions in the law, since he is always the same and unchanging.

For when he says, "Where have you laid Lazarus?" he is ignorant neither of the Gospel nor of the Old Testament. He says, "Where have you laid him?" because he wants to rebuke the women, who had not shown even a faith equal to that of the Shunammite woman. Yet she had faith in a man, namely Elisha the holy prophet, while Martha and her sister had faith in God.

And when he says, "Who touched me?" he does not say it out of ignorance. He says it to persuade the woman to confess of her own accord, so that the Son of God would not bear witness about himself but would be glorified by others.

And when he says, "Do you have loaves with you?" he says it so that everyone might be shown how few the loaves were, and the greatness of his miracle might be marveled at, since so great a crowd was fed with so few loaves. And when he says, "Whom are you seeking?"
he shows that those seeking him have been deceived. They are "seeking Jesus," a name that means "physician" and "savior," so that when they kill him they would forfeit the salvation he brings.

109. So we have shown that what is said about our Lord's incarnate dispensation is said in a human way, yet not without foreknowledge. No right-minded person would say that he did not know where they had laid Lazarus, since he was near the place, even though he asked in the way we have described. Earlier, while he was far away in Galilee, he had made known of himself that Lazarus [?]. In the same way, then, we sensibly resolve these questions about the Old Testament.
When God said, "Adam, where are you?" he was not speaking as one who did not know. He was showing from what a height to what a depth of shame Adam had fallen.
And "Where is Abel your brother?" means: the one whom you ought always to have carried in your arms and always stayed beside has been thrown to the ground by you.

He shows from what follows that he did not ask out of ignorance but as a rebuke, for he says, "Cursed is the ground in your works, and cursed are you from the ground, which opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand."

"For behold," he says, "his voice cries out to me." And he did not say "Where is Sarah your wife?" out of ignorance. How could he not know, when he knew that she was laughing inside the house? So he did not ask out of ignorance. He asked so as to set her conduct before her daughters who "profess godliness," for them to learn from it whenever they try to serve the saints from the fruit of their own labors.

For although she was busy with so great a service, making the unleavened cakes baked in the ashes herself and preparing such a large meal together with her own servants, she did not look upon the faces of those she was serving. In this she left our generations an example of becoming modesty. This will be enough as a reply to the objections of the empty-minded.

110. And suppose they say: "A fine God, the God of the law! He cheated the Egyptians, and taught his own people to plunder them when they went out of the land of Egypt." The fools do not know that with God nothing is lost, that there is righteous judgment, and that "God is not mocked."

For what did the Egyptians imagine when they demanded that the Jews do this work for them without pay, and not for a few years but for two hundred and fifteen, along with † the two hundred and fifteen years of Joseph [?]?

For a sojourn of four hundred and thirty years had been fixed for Abraham and his descendants, as it says, "Your offspring will be sojourners in a foreign land." At that time what had been fixed was being fulfilled.

So in his compassion God divided the years of their sojourn. He first spent two hundred and fifteen years while they were still in their own land [?], and he assigned the other two hundred and fifteen to those who went into Egypt.

The number of these years is reckoned as follows. It was then Abraham's seventy-fifth year. From Abraham's seventy-fifth year to the birth of Isaac there are [?] years. Isaac begets Jacob in his sixtieth year, and that makes [?] years. Jacob, at the age of [?], begets Levi, and that makes 174 years. Levi, at the age of forty-four, begets Kohath. In the [?]-seventh year of Levi, Jacob goes down into Egypt, and that makes two hundred and eleven years. After their entry into Egypt there are another four years, and the two hundred and fifteen are completed.

From this point the remaining two hundred and fifteen years of the Israelites' sojourn are counted again. Kohath, after the descent into Egypt, in his sixty-fifth year begets Abraham, the father of Moses. So from the first Abraham, from his seventy-fifth year, to the birth of the last Abraham there are [?] years, and from the descent into Egypt sixty-five years.
Abraham, at the age of seventy, begets Moses. That makes 350 years from the first Abraham, and 135 years from the descent into Egypt.
Moses, in his thirtieth year, crosses the Red Sea, going out of Egypt together with the Israelites. That makes 380 years from the great Abraham, and 165 from the descent into Egypt.

They spent the remaining fifty years after crossing the Red Sea before arriving in Palestine. This was not because of the length of the road, but because they were fighting and being hindered by the nations they met along the way.

So from the seventy-fifth year of the great Abraham, when this prophecy was given to him by God, to Moses and the arrival of the sons of Israel in Palestine there are 430 years, and from the descent into Egypt to their arrival in Palestine 215 years.

111. Since, then, the Jews had worked for so many years without pay, was it not just, before God and men, that they should be given their wages, even if only at the end? So God was not unjust in bringing his own people out of there with spoils.
If anyone doubts that the years are counted this way, let him hear Moses saying, "The dwelling of the sons of Israel in the land of Canaan and in the land of Egypt was 430 years."

Since the Lord saw to it that they received a most just wage, what empty objection is still left to those who wish to heap blame on the holy God? No one could ever find fault with the true God; those who find fault are only finding fault with themselves.

They also put forward another empty objection, similar to the first: "A fine God, the God of the law! He cheated the Canaanites in order to give their place to the Israelites, 'houses which they had not built, and olive groves and fig orchards and vineyards which they had not planted.'"

To them I will say: You fools! If God were like a man, the things said or done today would pass away, and he would keep none of them in mind. But since God "is God and not man," he does not forget what is brought before him, and he avenges it for many generations. If they do not know about this matter, let them learn.

112. Everyone knows that righteous Noah became the remnant of the world after the flood. When he and his three sons were left, he, being righteous, tried to make his children devout, so that they would not fall into the same evils as those who perished in the flood. He not only taught them piety by his words, but also required each of them to swear an oath of goodwill toward his brother.
And since he had been appointed heir of the world by God, he divided the whole world among his three sons. He divided it into lots and assigned each portion to each son by lot.

To Shem, the firstborn, fell the lot stretching in length from Persia and Bactria to India, and in breadth from [?] to the region of Rhinocorura. This Rhinocorura lies between Egypt and Palestine, opposite the Red Sea.
To Ham, the second, fell the southern parts, from the same Rhinocorura to Gadeira. To Japheth, the third, fell the northern parts, from Media to Gadeira and Rhinocorura.
113. To Shem were born children and children's children, twenty-five of them, up to the time when the languages were divided. They are scattered among languages, tribes and kingdoms.

Their names are these: Elymaeans, Paeonians, Lazones, Cossaeans, Gasphenes, Palestinians, Indians, Syrians, Arabs who are also called Tai, Arians, Mardians, Hyrcanians, Magusaeans, Assyrians, Germanians, Lydians, Mesopotamians, Hebrews, Coelenians, Bactrians, Adiabenians, Camelians, Saracens, Scythians, † Chiones [?], Gymnosophists, Chaldeans, Parthians, Eëtae, Cordylenians, Massynians, Phoenicians, Madienaeans, Commagenians, Dardanians, Elamasenians, Cedrusians, Elamites, Armenians, Cilicians, [Egyptians], Cappadocians, [Phoenicians], † Biones [?], Carians, Chalybes, Psyllites, Lazi, Mossynoeci, Iberians, Phrygians.

To Ham, the second, were born children and children's children, thirty-two of them, up to the same division of languages: Ethiopians, Troglodytes, Angaeans, Taienians, Sabines, Fish-eaters, Hellanicians, Egyptians, Phoenicians, Marmaridae, Carians, Psyllites, Mossynoeci, Phrygians, Macones, Macrones, Syrtites, Leptimagnites, Bithynians, Nomads, Lycians, Mariandynians, Pamphylians, † Moschesidians [?], Pisidians, Augalaeans, Cilicians, Maurusians, Cretans, Magardae, Numidians, Africans who are also called Byzacenians, Phasgenians, Mazices, Garamantes, Gaetulians, Blemmyes, Axumites. These hold the land from Egypt to the Ocean.

Their islands are: Cossyra, Lopadusa, Gaulos, Rhide, Melite, Corcyra, Mene, Sardinia, Gortyna, Crete, Glaucus, Rhide, Thera, Carianthus, Astypalaea, Chios, Lesbos, Tenedos, Imbros, Iasos, Samos, Cos, Cnidus, Nisyros, Megiste, and Cyprus.

To Japheth, the third, were born children and children's children, fifteen of them, up to the same division of languages: Medes, Albanians, Gargians, Armenians, Arraeans, Amazons, Coli, Corzenians, Beneagenians, Cappadocians, Galatians, Paphlagonians, Mariandynians, Tibarenians, Chalybes, Mossynoeci, Colchians, Melanchenians, Sauromatians, Germans, Maeotians, Scythians, Taurians, Thracians, Bastarnae, Illyrians, Macedonians, Greeks, Libyans, † Phrygians, Pannonians, Istrians, Vennians, Daunians, Iapygians, Calabrians, Hippici, Latins who are also called Romans, Tyrrhenians, Gauls who are also called Celts, Ligurians, Celtiberians, Iberians, Gauls, Aquitanians, Illyrians, Basantes, Cannii, Cartani, Lusitanians, Vaccaei, Britons, Scots, Spaniards.
Their islands are: Britain, Sicily, Euboea, Rhodes, Chios, Lesbos, Cythera, Zacynthus, Cephallenia, Ithaca, Corcyra, Cyprus.

Sometimes the name of a nation or island is listed twice, once in one son's lot and again in another's. This is because of shared borders, or because of colonies founded over time, or because Ham grasped and seized parts of Shem's territory. Let no one be surprised or doubt it.

114. These nations, then, arose in this way from the three sons of Noah, and the world was divided in three among the three sons. As I said before, their father required an oath from them that none of them would encroach on his brother's lot.
In the oath they declared that whoever broke its terms should be utterly destroyed, together with all his descendants.
Palestine and all the lands near it fell to Shem's lot. But Canaan, the son of Ham, being greedy, later invaded the land of the Palestinians, that is, Judea, and seized it. God was patient,

granting them time for repentance, so that the descendants of Ham might repent and give back their own allotment to the descendants of Shem. But they did not repent; instead they chose to fill up their measure.
Then, many generations later, God, being just, avenged the breaking of the oath. For this was how the measure of the Amorites had to be filled up.
Shem begets Arphaxad; Ham begets Canaan. And Canaan, after his act of greed, begets the Amorite, the Girgashite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, the Arkite, the Arvadite and the Sidonian.

The generations up to the vindication of Shem are counted as follows. Shem, the one who was cheated, begets Arphaxad, as we said. Arphaxad begets Cainan, Cainan begets Shelah, Shelah begets Eber, and the building of the tower takes place. Eber begets Peleg, and the division of the earth and of the languages takes place. Peleg begets Reu, Reu begets Serug, Serug begets Nahor, Nahor begets Terah, Terah begets Abraham, Abraham begets Isaac, Isaac begets Jacob, who was named Israel and from whom the Israelites come. Jacob begets Judah, Judah begets Perez, Perez begets Hezron, Hezron begets Ram, Ram begets Amminadab, Amminadab begets Nahshon, and Nahshon begets Salmon. This is the line of those descended from Shem.

These, then, had been wronged by the sons of Ham and robbed of their own place. God avenges them by destroying the descendants of Canaan according to their own oath, and the seed of Shem recovers its own land. So God did no wrong, but gave each party what was just; "for God is not mocked," as I said before.

115. At the exodus, then, when God was about to join a congregation to himself, he says to Moses, "Take the sandals off your feet." For everyone who is about to approach pure washings first takes off his shoes.

But a long time passed, and each of us "went astray in his own way," and this congregation remained in its own evils. So God did not yet reveal "the washing of regeneration" but put it off for many years, and later revealed the all-holy washing to the holy church. In Moses

he took off the sandals. In the prophets he stripped off the outer tunic, leaving Jeremiah only a loincloth. In John he exchanged all the garments of the world and reclothed him in camel's hair. In the Savior himself and his disciples he stripped off "the form of the world," and from above, from heaven, after the cleansing, he clothed them with the garment "of fire and Spirit."

But although the Israelites saw his grace, they did not recognize that he is God. That is why the prophet lamented over them with reproach, because of the dishonor they would do to the Savior, saying, "Is this how you repay the Lord, you foolish and senseless people?"
For they did not recognize that he was the one with whom, in the beginning, the Father took counsel when he said, "Let us make man according to our image and likeness."

For "let us make" does not signify a single person. Rather, the Father took counsel with the Son and the Holy Spirit; "for by the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the breath of his mouth all their host."

Nor did they understand the one who says plainly in the same book, "The Lord rained fire and brimstone on Sodom and Gomorrah from the Lord out of heaven." "The Lord rained fire" means the one who had come to Abraham; "from the Lord out of heaven" means the one who had sent him.

Nor did they recognize him as the one who was bringing them out of Egypt, nor did they understand the prophet who says, "And you, Bethlehem, are by no means the least." (For how could one call a city the least when it held the one whom heaven and all things could not hold?) And he says, "From you shall come forth for me a ruler." But if he comes from Bethlehem and is a man, how is he spoken of as God?

116. What troubles them is that he is God and man. For in the same passage it says [?], "His goings forth are from the beginning, from the creation of the world"; and this no longer belongs to a man, but to God.

Nor do they remember that "Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel." And "they shall call" signifies the way of the holy and faithful, the children of the church.

For when the Lord-murdering Jews question them about the Savior, asking, "How can you believe in one who was crucified?" they confess him [?], and the Jews hear from these same faithful: "Among you he was crucified, but with us he is God."

But they did not listen to David and did not recognize his word, which he spoke as he saw in the Holy Spirit, trembling at the dispensation of the Lord himself that was to come: "The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand," and the rest.

So "the ancient Sabbaths have passed away," and a true Sabbath is proclaimed among us. The first circumcision, which cut one very small member, has ceased; but the heavenly circumcision, which circumcises the whole body, is fully at work.

For the waters and the holy invocation do not act on just one member of a person. Rather, [the whole] body of the person is sealed, cleansed and circumcised, and set free from all evils. The holy church, then, has received these mysteries.

But fierce enemies also rose up against her, called "members of the household," yet not belonging to the true faith of the Lord's apostles ("for if they had been of them, they would have remained with them").

Being bastards and a mixed multitude, they again long with an evil craving for the Egyptian food of fish and cucumbers, blaspheming the Son of God up and down. Some are the Ario-maniacs, whom we have already pilloried in our earlier discourses, and others are Sabellians.

The Sabellians deny altogether that the Son and the Holy Spirit exist. They say that the Son is the Father, that the Father himself is the Son, and that the Holy Spirit is the Father himself, so that there is no Son and no Holy Spirit. They are exposed as second Jews and Lord-murderers.

The Ario-maniacs are the most impious of all. They dare to divide and estrange the Son from the Father's essence, and do not allow that the Son is equal in honor with the Father or that he was begotten from the Father's essence.

There are others, their offspring, whom I counted earlier, along with the others listed before, [?] as being like the Jews: those who blaspheme the Holy Spirit, second Sadducees and Samaritans, dead [?] and faithless.

117. But so that we do not draw out at length, "with ink and paper," the testimonies against them and weary our readers, for the Sabellians, besides the other testimonies, the testimony of the Jordan will be enough, as I have already said.

For the Son truly comes to the Jordan, God who has become man. He did not undergo change but took flesh. He did not come from a man's seed but took a body from the holy Virgin, conceived through the Holy Spirit: a complete body, that is, a complete man in soul and body.

So God-made-man came to John at the Jordan, one and the same Son and Christ and Lord. And the Father cries out from above, bearing witness to the Son who had come to the Jordan: "This is my beloved Son."

And the Holy Spirit came down in the form of a dove upon him when he had gone down into the waters, to make them pure for those who would be baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

For the Arians, besides what has already been said, it will be enough that the Son said, "I am in the Father and the Father is in me." Here he showed that the Son is equal to the Father and truly his own.

For the offspring of the Arians, who blaspheme the Holy Spirit, two testimonies already set out earlier will be enough, along with the others. One is from Daniel and runs as follows: in the furnace of fire Shadrach,

Meshach and Abednego, as they praise God, include with themselves the whole creation of God and say, "Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord." They listed the heavens and angels, moon and sun and powers, earth and sea and everything in them, but nowhere did they count the Son and the Holy Spirit among the creatures. And the Seraphim hallow the Trinity as equal. They say "Holy" not once, not twice, not four times, but three times.
118. Let Peter refute them again, when he rebukes Ananias and his wife and says, "You have tempted the Holy Spirit";

and he says, "You have not lied to a human being, but to God." The apostle also knows, as we have often said, that the Spirit is not alien to God, for he says, "He searches even the depths of God." Whatever is not from the essence of God cannot search the depths of God.

We, however, know the Father as Father, the Son as Son, the Holy Spirit as Holy Spirit: a Trinity in unity. For there is one unity of Father and Son and Holy Spirit: one essence, one lordship, one will, one church, one baptism, one faith.
And let those cease who [speak] against the holy virgin and pure bride of Christ, that is, our mother the holy church [?].
For her children received from holy fathers, that is, from the holy apostles, a faith to keep, and at the same time to hand on and proclaim to their own children.
You yourselves are her sons, most honoured brothers; hand this teaching on to your own children.

Say these things in this way, and things like them from the divine Scriptures [?], to confirm both yourselves and those who hear you; teaching, guiding and instructing, do not cease, you who are faithful and orthodox, to keep this holy faith of the catholic church, as the holy and only virgin of God received it from the holy apostles of the Lord.

And so, with each of the catechumens who are about to come to the holy washing, you ought not only to proclaim [?] what is to be believed to your own sons in the Lord, but also to teach them expressly, as the one mother of us all, both yours and ours, to say:
We believe in one God, the Father Almighty, maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible;

and in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, begotten of the Father before all ages, that is, from the essence of the Father, light from light, true God from true God, begotten, not made, of one essence with the Father, through whom all things came to be, both those in the heavens and those on earth; who for us human beings and for our salvation came down from the heavens and was made flesh of the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary and became man, and was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate, and suffered and was buried, and rose on the third day according to the Scriptures, and ascended into the heavens, and is seated at the right hand of the Father, and is coming again with glory to judge the living and the dead; of whose kingdom there will be no end;

and in the Holy Spirit, the Lord and giver of life, who proceeds from the Father, who together with the Father and the Son is worshipped and glorified, who spoke through the prophets; in one holy, catholic and apostolic church;
we confess one baptism for the forgiveness of sins; we look for the resurrection of the dead and the life of the age to come. Amen.

But those who say, "There was a time when he was not," and "Before he was begotten he was not," or that he came to be from things that are not, or who claim that the Son of God is of another hypostasis or essence, or is mutable, these the catholic and apostolic church anathematizes.
And this faith was handed down from the holy apostles, and [?] in the church in the holy city by all the holy bishops of that time together, more than three hundred in number [?].

119. But since in our own generation certain other heresies have sprung up one after another, that is, in the time of the emperors Valentinian and Valens, in the tenth year of their reign, and again in the sixth year of Gratian, that is, in the ninetieth year of Diocletian the tyrant,

for this reason you and we and all the orthodox bishops, and in short the whole holy catholic church, in answer to the heresies that have sprung up, speak as follows, in keeping with the faith set out above by those holy fathers, and especially to those who are coming to the holy washing, so that they may proclaim and say this:
We believe in one God, the Father Almighty, maker of all things invisible and visible;

and in one Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the only-begotten, begotten of God the Father, that is, from the essence of the Father, God from God, light from light, true God from true God, begotten, not made, of one essence with the Father, through whom all things came to be, both those in the heavens and those on

earth, visible and invisible; who for us human beings and for our salvation came down and was made flesh, that is, was perfectly born of holy Mary the ever-virgin through the Holy Spirit; who became man, that is, took a complete human being, soul and body and mind and everything that a human being is, without sin;

not [born] from the seed of a man, nor [dwelling] in a man, but forming flesh anew into himself in one holy unity; not as he breathed and spoke and worked in the prophets, but becoming man completely.

For "the Word became flesh," not by undergoing change, nor by converting his own divinity into humanity, but by uniting into one his own [?] holy perfection and divinity. For there is one [?] Lord Jesus Christ, and not two: the same is God, the same is Lord, the same is King.

The same suffered in the flesh, and rose, and ascended into the heavens in the very body, and sat down in glory at the right hand of the Father, and is coming in the very body in glory to judge the living and the dead; of whose kingdom there will be no end.
And in the Holy Spirit, who spoke in the Law and preached in the prophets, came down upon the Jordan, speaks in the apostles, and dwells in the saints.

And we believe in him thus: that he is the Holy Spirit, the Spirit of God, the perfect Spirit, the Spirit Paraclete, uncreated, proceeding from the Father and receiving from the Son, and [?] believed in.

We believe in one catholic and apostolic church, and in one baptism of repentance, and in the resurrection of the dead and the just judgement of souls and bodies, and in the kingdom of heaven, and in eternal life.

But those who say that there was a time when the Son or the Holy Spirit was not, or that he came to be from things that are not, or who claim that the Son of God or the Holy Spirit is of another hypostasis or essence, or [?] changeable, these the catholic and apostolic church anathematizes, the mother of both you and us. And again, we anathematize those who do not confess the resurrection of the dead, and all the heresies that do not stem from this orthodox faith.

Since you and your children, most blessed ones, believe in this way and carry out the commandments that flow from this faith, we hope that you will pray for us always, that we may have a share and a portion in the same

faith and in the portion of its commandments. And pray for us, you and everyone who believes in this way and keeps the commandments of the Lord, in Christ Jesus our Lord, through whom and with whom be glory to the Father with the Holy Spirit for ever and ever. Amen.

This is as far, beloved brothers, as our littleness and the feeble power of our understanding has been compelled to reach, since your noble goodness urged us to present this, incapable though we are and beyond our own measure, so that in straining forward we stand in need of help. But the Faithful One in heaven knows all things.

Peace, then, to everyone who walks by this rule of this true and orthodox faith, and upon the Israel of God. Greet all the saints in the Lord. The servants of the Lord greet you, and especially I, Anatolius, who wrote out this book, the discourse entitled Ancoratus; and I pray that you may fare well in the Lord.
